chapter: New Orleans, Havana and back to New York
title: Why the band left New Orleans: Seymour Weiss and Milton Romer
summary: Hotel owner Seymour Weiss complained about the volume and Romer invented a Miami Beach job so the band would give notice.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: I see. And how about -- I'm looking for which book I found it in. I think it was George Simon's book. Said the reason you left there was that they wanted you to play softer and you wouldn't, and so they set up some guys in the red light district, some guys in your band, and busted them, and then the band had to leave town. Is that right?

No. There was a setup of a kind, but the way it happened was Seymour Weiss called Milton Romer and said, 'Look, will you get this band out of here? They're driving me crazy.' So Milton went along, he called and said, 'Look, I've got a job for you in Miami Beach. Would you like
to work there?" And I said, "Oh, yeah." He said, "Well, give your notice." He was in cahoots with Weiss, see? There wasn't any job in Miami Beach. We gave our notice, and of course we were out.
Oh. And then where did you go?
